title: Infinitesimal pushout gluing of proper-support flat families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. Let $Z\to Z'$ be a nilpotent thickening of $S$-schemes and $Z\to Y$ an affine morphism [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and suppose $Y'=Y\amalg_Z Z'$ is their scheme pushout. A nilpotent thickening is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] defined by a nilpotent ideal. Restriction induces an equivalence $\mathcal C(Y')\simeq\mathcal C(Y)\times_{\mathcal C(Z)}\mathcal C(Z')$. The right side consists of two objects with a specified isomorphism on $Z$, and compatible pairs of arrows. In particular this holds for spectra of ring fibre products $A\times_D D'$ when $D'\to D$ is surjective with square-zero kernel.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-affine-thickening-pushout], the scheme pushout $Y'$ is also a pushout for algebraic-space targets and $Y\hookrightarrow Y'$ is a thickening. Thus a compatible pair $b_Y:Y\to B$, $b_{Z'}:Z'\to B$ has a unique extension $b:Y'\to B$. An isomorphism over $Z$ in the stated fibre product includes equality of the two maps to $B$. Fixing $b$, write $V=X\times_BY'$ and $V_T=V\times_{Y'}T$ for $T=Y,Z,Z'$. By the fibre-product universal property these are canonically $X\times_BT$, and all subsequent restrictions use these identifications. It suffices to glue the modules for each fixed $b$; different maps $b$ cannot be connected by arrows in the fibre groupoid.

For every scheme $T\to B$, the map $X_T\to T$ is locally of finite presentation, hence locally of finite type. Here is the chart justification needed for the later inputs. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $E\to B$ and one $U\to X\times_BE$. The scheme map $U\to E$ is locally of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. After base change to $T$, [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] gives atlases $E_T\to T$ and $U\times_EE_T\to X_T\times_TE_T$. On affine opens of $U,E$, [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] gives finite presentations of the coordinate algebras. Tensoring these presentations with coordinate algebras of affine opens of $E_T$ preserves finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition]. These affine fibre-product charts cover the source, so [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] gives local finite presentation of the base-changed chart map. The chart criterion gives the assertion for $X_T\to T$. A finitely presented algebra is finitely generated by its finitely many polynomial generators, giving local finite type on the same charts.

Apply [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support] to $V\to Y'$ and to each restriction of the base. Its local-finite-type hypothesis was verified in Step 2. Thus a finitely presented flat module with a proper carrier restricts to modules satisfying all three conditions over $Y,Z,Z'$. The canonical pullback-composition isomorphisms give the specified comparison over $Z$. Pullback sends an isomorphism to an isomorphism, so this defines the restriction functor in the statement.

Given a compatible object on the right with its fixed map $b$, apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-flat-module-pushout] with $(T_0,T_1,T_2,P,V)=(Z,Z',Y,Y',X\times_BY')$. It produces a quasi-coherent module $M$ flat over $Y'$ and identifications of its restrictions with the two given modules, inducing the specified overlap isomorphism. Step 2 supplies the local finite presentation of $V\to Y'$, so the finite-presentation criterion of that node makes $M$ finitely presented. Proper support remains to be checked; it was not a conclusion of the module-patching node.

Let $W'\hookrightarrow V$ be the closed subspace defined by $\operatorname{Ann}(M)$, whose existence and quasi-coherence are given by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support]. Its point set is $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$: on etale affine charts the finite-module formula of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] identifies both with the zero locus of the annihilator, and [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support] identifies the chart supports with the inverse image of the geometric support. This applies also to the given restriction $M_Y$. Let $W=W'\times_{Y'}Y$. By [lem-sfb-space-thickening-base-change], $W\hookrightarrow W'$ and $V_Y\hookrightarrow V$ are thickenings. By [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-support-pullback], $|W|=\operatorname{Supp}(M_Y)$ inside $|V_Y|$. All these modules have finite type because they have finite presentation. The given proper carrier of $M_Y$ implies that its annihilator support is proper by [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support]. Its point set is $|W|$, so [lem-sfb-space-proper-support-closed-operations] implies that $W\to Y$ is proper as well; this uses the local finite type of $V_Y\to Y$ from Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0CZI, lemma-module-support-proper-over-base; Tag 0CZC, lemma-closed-proper-over-base; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 07TZ, lemma-support-finite-type. Proper-support condition implicit in the last sentence of Tag 08LQ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-thickening-topological-properties] to $W\to Y$ and $W'\to Y'$, using the two thickenings established in Steps 1 and 5. Properness of $W\to Y$ gives quasi-compactness, separatedness and universal closedness of $W'\to Y'$. It is locally of finite type: $W'$ is closed in $V$, and on affine scheme charts its coordinate algebra is a quotient of a locally finitely presented, hence finitely generated, algebra over the base. The same finite set of algebra generators generates this quotient. Thus [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties] makes $W'\to Y'$ proper. Finally [lem-sfb-space-module-proper-carrier-support] converts properness of the annihilator support to the required proper-carrier formulation for $M$. No flatness of $V$ or of the support, and no Noetherian hypothesis, has been used.

proof.text: For any two objects over the same $b$, [lem-sfb-space-relative-flat-module-pushout] gives a bijection on all module Hom sets with compatible pairs of homomorphisms on the two pieces. A compatible pair of isomorphisms lifts to an isomorphism: lift the pair of inverse maps too, and faithfulness makes their two composites identities. This proves full faithfulness on the fibre groupoids. Steps 4--6 prove essential surjectivity, including the prescribed overlap identification. Step 1 accounts for the maps to $B$. Hence restriction is the asserted equivalence of groupoids.

For the last assertion take $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}D$ and $Z'=\operatorname{Spec}D'$. The surjection $D'\to D$ with square-zero kernel gives precisely the required nilpotent thickening. Every map between affine schemes is affine. By [lem-sfb-affine-closed-pinching-pushout], their scheme pushout is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\times_DD')$. Its universal property also supplies its $S$-structure from those of the pieces, so the equivalence already proved applies.
